tollington.notes: 8 giant screens (not 14), Sky+TNT, every live game. Home-cooked food + Thai fusion, Sunday roasts. Large front terrace. Voted best Arsenal pub by Gooner readers. 115 Hornsey Rd.

patch.food.note: Home-cooked pub food with a Thai fusion menu and Sunday roasts, eaten in the bar

twelve-pins.notes: 6 big screens plus screens in the beer garden; large front and back gardens; Arsenal, GAA and major sports; pies, roasts, spice bags.

famous-cock.notes: Multi-screen, Sky and TNT, often two games at once, loud. Booths at front, outside area at back. 8 min to Emirates.

faltering-fullback.notes: Big screens for live sport with a dedicated 'Sin Bin' sports area; rugby hotspot; award-winning multi-level garden; Thai menu.

bank-of-friendship.notes: TV for sport in saloon bar, quiet public bar. Paved rear garden with open fires. Open mic Thursdays, live sessions summer Sundays. Arsenal memorabilia, very busy on home days.

bricklayers.notes: Home supporters only on match days. 3 indoor screens plus 50-inch TVs in the outdoor seating with its own bar. Pool, darts.

antwerp-arms.notes: Community-owned since 2015, CAMRA North London Pub of the Year 2020, Redemption beers, beer garden, quiz Tuesdays, 200m from the ground and busy on match days. Screen count unconfirmed.

beehive.notes: Sky and TNT; outside bar and BBQ on Spurs match days; heated, sheltered garden; football tables; British menu (burgers, fish and chips); Fri/Sat open until 2am.

patch.food.note: Traditional British menu from the Bruce Stove kitchen, burgers and fish and chips, BBQ outside on match days

butchers-hook.notes: Greene King. Opposite Stamford Bridge; Chelsea FC founded here in 1905 (then the Rising Sun). Sky, TNT, BBC and ITV on big screens. Family and dog friendly, restaurant section.

chelsea-pensioner.notes: 358 Fulham Rd, 2 min from Stamford Bridge. Live sport on screens, DJ before kick-off on home games. Otherwise quiz, karaoke, comedy, live music, pool and a sunny garden.

imperial-arms.notes: Designated dining area beside a weatherproof year-round covered garden. Family-style Sunday roasts. Football-heavy crowd on match days.

boleyn-tavern.notes: Own site: no mention of live sport, screens, Sky or TNT. Hours Mon-Wed 4-11, Thu 12-11, Fri-Sat 12-12, Sun 12-10. Grade II, CAMRA historic interior, 1.5m Remarkable Pubs restoration 2021, open kitchen and dining area, three cask ales, garden. Treat as a heritage food pub with West Ham history, not a match-day screen pub.

patch.tip: West Ham's old cathedral, restored to its 1899 glory: seven bars, etched glass and a stained-glass skylight over the dining room. Go for the building and the roast, not the screens.

carpenters-arms.notes: Spiritual home of West Ham fans since the stadium move. Large patio garden, vertical drinking space, West Ham decor. 15 min walk to London Stadium, Stratford High St 350m.

denmark-arms.notes: Grade II, 381 Barking Rd. Closed 2018 after the stadium move; reopened Nov 2018 under Antic as a craft-and-food pub. Sky TV listed. Heritage West Ham pub rather than a match-day fortress now.

patch.food.note: Antic kitchen, pub classics and roasts

clifton-arms.notes: Victorian pub c.1865, 2 min from Selhurst Park, the unofficial home pub for Palace fans. Real ale. Open 12-23 Mon-Sat.

prince-george.notes: Live sport on three screens, welcomes home and away fans, quiz Monday.

crabtree.notes: 4 Rainville Rd. Seven HD screens inside plus outdoor screens in the enormous riverside garden; glazed colonnade terrace on the Thames. Pre and post match for Craven Cottage, Boat Race, tournaments.

temperance.notes: Grade II 1910 former billiards hall, 90 Fulham High St. Now a live-sports pub that hosts AWAY fans on Craven Cottage match days, with a very large number of TVs. Comfort food: mac and cheese, wings, burgers, stone-baked pizza. Three pool tables, darts.

patch.food.note: Comfort food: loaded burgers, wings, mac and cheese and stone-baked pizzas, served in the hall

griffin.notes: The surviving corner pub of old Griffin Park. Friendly local, small shaded patio garden, Bees fans watch games on the screens pre and post match. Featured in Green Street.

globe-brentford.notes: Victorian 1888 pub, 104 Windmill Rd. Fuller's ales. Live Sky and TNT across 6 big screens, live music every weekend, quiz Wednesday, pool, fresh organic kitchen. Supporter of Brentford FC and London Irish.

patch.food.note: Fresh food cooked to order from sustainable, organic and free-range ingredients
patch.tip: Six screens with Sky and TNT, live music at weekends and a proper kitchen. Bees and London Irish both drink here.

crown-sceptre.notes: Fuller's, 57 Melina Rd, in the shadow of Loftus Road. Big screens, real ales, British pub fare plus Thai dishes, well-regarded Sunday roast, heated garden. Family and dog friendly. Filming location for Minder and Steptoe and Son.

springbok.notes: Renamed the Queens Tavern in 2016. Now a supporters' bar: open on match days only and for home fans only. Darts teams.

patch.name: Queens Tavern (ex Springbok)
patch.tip: Yards from Loftus Road and now a supporters' bar: match days only, home fans only. Not a Tuesday-night pint.

blue-anchor.notes: 251 Southwark Park Rd, built 1875. Craft Union since 2021. Live sport on TV daily, very busy on Millwall home days, dartboards, wall of framed Millwall shirts. London Pride, Doom Bar. Thu-Sat until midnight.

royal-oak-charlton.notes: 300 yards from The Valley, the default pre-match pub, packed on match days. Large screens, beer garden, occasional DJs, darts, Charlton memorabilia.

coach-horses-leyton.notes: 391 High Rd Leyton, pub since 1863, independent. Up to 25 draught beers and cask, authentic Sri Lankan street food. Main bar plus small back dining area. Partially covered garden. Home fans only on Orient home days (ticket shown at the door), six screens indoor and outdoor. Live music Fridays. Family and dog friendly.

patch.food.note: Authentic Sri Lankan street food from the kitchen, eaten in the back dining area, the bar or the covered garden

sports-bar-victoria.notes: Upstairs at Victoria Station. Huge array of screens, interactive video wall, nine bookable booths each with its own TV. Open from 7am with breakfast.

f3k.notes: 171 North End Rd, next to West Kensington station. 38 screens plus two projector screens, Sky and TNT, all national and international football plus rugby, NFL, boxing, F1. Multiple Sports Pub of the Year wins at the Great British Pub Awards. Cocktails and food.

greenwood.notes: Opposite Victoria Station, calls itself London's biggest premium sports bar. 30+ UHD screens and a 150-inch TV wall across two floors, 200-capacity private room, sun-trap terrace, breakfast to dinner.

belushis-lb.notes: Multi-screen with two huge projectors; The Dugout downstairs with 4K screens, Sky Q and Dolby Atmos. Open till 2am Sun-Thu and 3am Fri-Sat. Live music, DJs and karaoke after the match.

bar-kick.notes: Now Bar Kick at The Shoreditch Arms (Urban Pubs and Bars). Twelve big screens across three floors, up to three games at once. Six championship-grade football tables at 1 pound a game. Dirty burgers and fried chicken, craft beer, cocktails, comedy nights.

patch.food.note: Dirty burgers and proper fried chicken, eaten wherever you can see a screen

boxpark-wembley.notes: 20,000 sq ft events space by Wembley Stadium, huge screens and sound system, 20+ street-food vendors, PlayBox bar upstairs, club room, karaoke and comedy nights. Pre-match fan zone needs a valid match ticket plus general admission.

boxpark-croydon.notes: Shows every televised Crystal Palace game plus the big tournaments. Most games have free and paid tickets; walk-ins welcome but a digital Black Card sign-up is needed for entry.

kings-arms-wandsworth.notes: 94-96 Wandsworth High St. Young's. Extensive garden with huts running alongside the River Wandle, semi-private Moatside garden area. Screens spread throughout for rugby and football. British classics, Young's ales and craft.

ship-wandsworth.notes: 18th-century pub at 41 Jews Row by Wandsworth Bridge. Riverside terrace, summer outdoor BBQ, classic bar menu. Shows major European and domestic fixtures including TNT Champions League and Premier League. Riverside cabins for private parties seat up to 15, each with a plasma screen. Private boat dock.

patch.food.note: Classic pub menu of burgers and sausages with a summer BBQ on the terrace; bookable riverside cabins for groups

pub-on-the-park.notes: 19 Martello St, behind London Fields station. Fairy-lit wrap-around terrace with heaters and large outdoor screens; seven TV screens in the main bar often showing different games at once. Resident DJs at weekends. Two private-hire spaces (70s speakeasy, retro basement) with no booking fee.

harp.notes: 47 Chandos Place. Fuller's since 2014. Ten handpumps of cask ale plus bag-in-box ciders and perries. CAMRA National Pub of the Year 2010 (first London winner), Evening Standard best pub 2019 and 2020. Two small rooms, no screens.

southampton-arms.notes: 139 Highgate Rd. Ale and cider house: 18 lines, all from independent UK producers. Cash only, vinyl only, meaty bar snacks, old piano, small beer garden. 5 min from Gospel Oak.

royal-oak-borough.notes: 44 Tabard St. Harvey's of Lewes' first London pub since 1997, Victorian two-bar layout, four handpumps in each bar, no machines, no music, just conversation. Daily Telegraph top-10 UK pub.

dove-hammersmith.notes: 19 Upper Mall, Grade II, Fuller's since 1796, early 18th century. Guinness record for the smallest bar room. Riverside terrace. Literary history (Greene, Hemingway, Morris next door). Food and restaurant.

mayflower.notes: 117 Rotherhithe St, origins 1550, claims oldest pub on the Thames. Wooden jetty over the river for about 30 drinkers. Upstairs candlelit restaurant with river views, private parties up to 60. Classic British menu, traditional ales, craft beer, local gins.

old-blue-last.notes: 38 Great Eastern St. Live music daily, free to 15 pounds, free jazz Sundays, free club nights Fri and Sat until 3am. Open until midnight Sun-Wed, 1am Thu, 2am Fri-Sat.

half-moon-putney.notes: Music venue since the 1960s, nine shows a week, reopened April 2026 after a revamp. Big screens inside for major events like the Boat Race. Americana-inspired menu and a Sunday roast.

patch.food.note: Americana-inspired menu and a well-regarded Sunday roast, eaten in the front bar

windmill-clapham.notes: Young's, dates from 1665, Grade II, with a 42-room hotel. Three large screens inside plus two outside in summer; Six Nations, Premier League, Wimbledon. Big garden with picnic benches, seasonal Burger Shack and Max's Shack cabin on match days. Conservatory restaurant, Sunday roasts.

patch.food.note: Conservatory restaurant with British classics and a strong Sunday roast; Burger Shack in the garden in summer

duke-edinburgh.notes: 204 Ferndale Rd, Grade II 1936 Truman's pub. One of south London's biggest gardens with covered heated areas and two outdoor bars. Huge projector screen in the garden plus seven big screens inside and out; Sky, TNT and Amazon. Pool table. Kitchen resident Jerk Valley (Caribbean), gluten-free menu, private hire.

patch.food.note: Jerk Valley's jerk chicken and Caribbean plates from the kitchen, eaten in the garden or the bar
patch.tip: One of the biggest beer gardens in south London with a proper jumbo screen outside. Tournament summers here are chaos in the best way.

prince-of-wales-brixton.notes: The Prince of Wales closed and the building reopened in April 2025 as Brixton Storeys, a 750-capacity club with a 24-hour licence. No longer a pub; removed from the list.

pineapple.notes: 51 Leverton St, Grade II, built c.1868. Thai kitchen, changing craft ales, fireplaces, conservatory and rear garden, 60-person upstairs function room, quiz Monday 9pm, very dog friendly.
